All use cases ↗

Define what is being transferred

Give Nema the work packet, handoff criteria, current state, and the teams involved. Name the deliverable and the point at which ownership should change. A handoff of an approved design differs from a request for engineering to explore options.

Include the intended audience. Private research, customer details, or commercial notes may need a restricted summary before entering a broader channel.

Preserve the decisions behind the work

The receiving team needs more than files. Ask Nema to list the decisions that shaped the deliverable, alternatives that were rejected when they matter, and links to the approved record. This reduces the chance that a settled choice is reopened because its reason was lost.

Keep proposals separate from decisions. A comment with strong wording is not automatically approval.

Expose dependencies and gaps

The checklist should name required inputs, current owners, due dates when confirmed, and the work each dependency blocks. Missing acceptance criteria or unclear scope should remain visible.

For example, an engineering handoff may include a final design but lack analytics events and error copy. Nema can identify those gaps from the supplied checklist. The project owner decides whether they block acceptance.

Confirm acceptance in Slack

Post the draft in a shared channel. The sending owner verifies completeness. The receiving owner asks questions and explicitly accepts the work, target, and next step. Ask Nema to post a revised summary of the agreed transfer in the thread.

This confirmation matters because a sent packet is not necessarily an accepted handoff. Any task reassignment in another system should follow the team's approved process.

Try one repeated transfer

Choose a common handoff, such as research to design or marketing to web production. Compare the packet with what the receiving team usually asks for after the fact. Add those durable requirements to the checklist, then test the revised flow on the next transfer.

Questions from delivery teams

When is a handoff complete?

Use the team's acceptance criteria and require the receiving owner to confirm. Uploading files alone does not complete the transfer.

How should sensitive notes be handled?

Create a summary for the receiving audience and keep restricted source material in its authorized location.

Can Nema resolve a scope dispute?

It can show the relevant decisions and conflicting records. The accountable project owners settle the scope.

After acceptance, keep later scope changes in the shared project record. The handoff captures what both teams agreed at transfer time; it should not silently expand whenever the receiving team discovers new work.
